checks: On the facet opposite i, each j≠i trace is a homothety of the facet about v_j, with area ratio (1−q_j)^(d−1) and centroid q_j v_j+(1−q_j)g_i. The i cap misses it because q_i>0.

Subtracting the constant-test equations for different facets equates the terms θ_j(1−q_j)^(d−1); each is β/d. The coordinate tests then give sum of q_j(v_j−g_i) over j≠i equal to zero. The coefficients obtained by subtracting their mean sum to zero, so affine independence makes the q_j on each facet equal.

Every pair belongs to some facet when d≥2. Thus all q_j=1/(d+1), which gives equal θ_j, and the constant equation yields β=(d/(d+1))^d. Exact rational arithmetic checked the resulting fraction for d=1 through 12.
In d=1 the two endpoint equations separately give θ_0=θ_1=β, so β=1/2 while the mark is unrestricted. This is exactly the separate endpoint argument in 00208e2b45f0da1a §2.

overlap.comparison: The accepted result forces canonical centroid caps from equality in an ordinary whole-body cap-volume profile. Here canonical directions are assumed and the equalities are affine moments on every full facet. Neither set of input conditions is supplied by the other.
The regular projected-contact result identifies full mixed section centroids under its own contact hypotheses and does not give the present facet-affine moment conclusion.

readability: The affine tests yield facet moments of the fixed response-weighted capture, independent of whether the original full coarea came from one or several fibers.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: Independent affine tests on all facets force the sharp simplex response, uniform weights, and the centroid mark in dimension at least two.
